title: Let's celebrate!
goals: Talk about plans and predictions with be going to (We're going to have a party).
Say who a gift is for, using indirect objects and pronouns (I'm going to buy her something special).
Choose between the present continuous and be going to for plans with a time or place.
Talk about celebrations and traditions: weddings, birthdays, festivals.
Say dates with months and ordinal numbers (on May 25th).
Use vague language (and stuff, and everything) and vague answers (It depends), and write invitations with good openings and closings.

learn.title: be going to: plans and predictions
learn.html:
Use be going to + base verb for future plans and for predictions based on what you can see. In Spanish it is like “voy a + verb”.

AffirmativeNegativeQuestion
I'm going to buy something special.You're not going to get a present.Are you going to have a party?
She's going to be 50.Marcos isn't going to have a party.What are you going to do tonight?
It's going to rain.They aren't going to come.Who's going to bring the cake?
  • Short answers: Yes, we are. / No, we're not. / No, he isn't.
  • When the question word is the subject, the order doesn't change: Who's going to go? What's going to happen?
  • After going to, the verb is in the base form (no -s or -ing).
  • Time expressions: tonight, tomorrow, next week, this weekend, in June.

watch.right: I'm going to buy a gift.

watch.wrong: She's going to buys a cake.
watch.right: She's going to buy a cake.
watch.why: After going to, use the base verb.

watch.wrong: Are you going have a party?
watch.right: Are you going to have a party?
watch.why: Don't forget the to in going to.

watch.wrong: What you are going to do tonight?
watch.right: What are you going to do tonight?
watch.why: In questions, be goes before the subject.

learn.title: Indirect objects: for whom
learn.html:
The indirect object answers the question “for whom?”. It goes before the direct object, without to or for: I'm going to buy my mother something special. If you already know who you are talking about, use a pronoun.

SubjectObject pronounExample
ImeMy sister is baking me a cake.
youyouI'm going to give you a book.
hehimI want to buy him something special.
sheherI'm going to get her some flowers.
weusGino is going to teach us Italian.
theythemLet's send them some flowers.

Common verbs: buy, give, get, send, bake, make, teach, show.

watch.wrong: I'm going to buy she a present.
watch.right: I'm going to buy her a present.
watch.why: After the verb, use the object pronoun (her), not the subject pronoun.

watch.wrong: She's going to give I a book.
watch.right: She's going to give me a book.

watch.wrong: They are going to give to us books.
watch.right: They are going to give us books.
watch.why: The indirect object goes without to, before the direct object.

learn.title: Plans: present continuous or be going to
learn.html:
For the future you have two options. The present continuous is used for plans that are already arranged, with a time, a place, or specific people. Be going to is used for general plans and for predictions.

UseExample
Plan with a time or place (present continuous)We're meeting friends at the restaurant at 8:30.
General plan (be going to)We're going to meet some friends at a restaurant.
Prediction (only be going to)It's going to snow tomorrow. It's going to be fun.
  • Often both forms work: I'm graduating next month. = I'm going to graduate next month.
  • Predictions use only be going to: It's going to rain. (not It's raining tomorrow).
  • With go and come, the continuous is common: I'm going to the doctor at four.

watch.wrong: Tomorrow I play soccer with my friends at 5:00.
watch.right: Tomorrow I'm playing soccer with my friends at 5:00.
watch.why: A plan with a time: present continuous.
A prediction is said with be going to.

watch.wrong: We meet my parents at 7:00 tonight.
watch.right: We're meeting my parents at 7:00 tonight.

watch.wrong: Are you do anything on Saturday?
watch.right: Are you doing anything on Saturday?

learn.title: Vague language and personal notes
learn.html:
In conversation, you sometimes don't give a complete list. Use vague expressions at the end of a list to mean “and things like that”.

  • and stuff (like that) — It's a festival. There are parades and stuff.
  • and things (like that) — You can eat tacos and things like that.
  • and everything — The kids wear outfits and makeup and everything.

When you can't or don't want to commit, use vague answers:

  • I don't know. / I'm not sure. / Maybe.
  • It depends. (+ a question or reason) — Are you going to the festival? — It depends. What is it exactly?

Personal notes and emails:

OpeningClosing
Less formalHi Roberto, / Dear Roberto,Take care, / See you, / Love,
More formalDear Ms. Benson,Best wishes, / Best regards, / All the best,

To invite someone: Would you like to come? Can you make it? Can I bring anything?

write.prompt: Write an invitation (60–100 words) to a celebration (a birthday, a wedding, or a party). For a friend, use Hi or Dear + name, and close with Take care, or See you,. Say when it is (date with on), where it is, what you are going to do (be going to), and what the guest can bring. Start with: Hi Ana, I'm having a party on ...
checklist: 60–100 words
A good opening and closing (Hi Ana, / Take care,)
Date with on and an ordinal or cardinal number (May 10th)
At least two plans with be going to
One plan with a time, using the present continuous
A question such as Can you make it?
write.model:
Hi Ana, I'm having a party on May 10th at my house. It's my birthday! The party is at 7 p.m. My address is 25 Reforma Street. We are going to eat a big cake, and we are going to play music and dance. My brother is going to cook tacos. I'm picking up the cake at 5 p.m., so I'm not going to be home early. Can you bring a drink or a snack for everybody? Can you make it?
Take care,
Luis

reading.title: My sister's wedding
paragraphs: Hi Ben, I'm writing with big news! My sister Paola is getting married on June 14th, and the whole family is already busy. The wedding ceremony is going to be at 5:00 in an old church in Puebla, and the reception is going to be in a garden near the city.

Everybody has a job. My parents are paying for the food, so there is going to be a lot of it: tacos, mole, cake and things like that. My cousin Hugo is going to bring his band. They play traditional music and everything. I'm making the invitations this week, and my brother Iván is buying the flowers on Friday. I'm also going to buy my sister something special. I don't know what yet. It depends on the price!

I'm sending you an invitation, too. Are you going to come? The party is going to be long. We're going to dance until midnight, and then we're going to see fireworks. The groom's relatives are arriving on the 12th, so we're having a big dinner with them that night. If you come early, you can stay at our house. Please tell me soon, because the hotel rooms in town are going to be expensive in June.

listening.title: A surprise party
listening.intro: Listen to the conversation between two friends. You can repeat it.

lines.text: Hi, Rosa! Are you doing anything on Saturday, the twentieth?
I don't know. It depends. Why?
It's Gina's thirtieth birthday, and we're going to have a surprise party at my house.
A surprise party? Wow! What time?
At seven. Her husband is bringing her at seven thirty.
Great. What are you going to make?
I'm going to make tacos and rice and things like that. Can you bring a cake?
Sure. I'm going to bake her a chocolate cake. Chocolate is her favorite.
Perfect. And what are we giving her?
I'm not sure. Maybe we can buy her tickets to a concert.
Good idea! Let's get her two tickets. She loves music and dancing and everything.
OK. I'm going to look online tonight, and I'm going to send you the prices tomorrow.
Thanks, Rosa. See you on Saturday!
